Subject: RFP: Commitment scenarios for dedicated inference (ApexBio)

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for taking this RFP. Attached is a short brief and our procurement questionnaire (apex_rfp_commitment_request.pdf). High-level asks:

- We need guidance on commitment sizing for a 12–24 month term with monthly billing.
- Primary models: a mix of Llama-3-ish 33B dense gen for chat and a smaller embeddings model for search.
- Expected steady-state: ~2.5M tokens/day (chat), average prompt + completion ~150 tokens, peak concurrency 240 concurrent requests.
- P95 latency targets: chat generation <= 150ms token latency, end-to-end 95th <= 350ms for single-turn requests.
- We expect to absorb burst traffic of up to 3x steady-state for up to 30 minutes during weekly batch jobs.

Please include explicit GPU type recommendations, how you map throughput to reservation tiers, and a fallback policy if reserved capacity is saturated. Also include a timeline for provisioning and any constraints on model quantization or topology.

Can you send an initial commitment staging plan and a GPU / SLO matrix by EOD tomorrow? If useful, we can schedule a technical workshop.

Best,
Maya Singh
Director, Cloud Infrastructure
ApexBio

Maya —

Thanks for the clear brief. We reviewed the numbers and sketched three commitment staging scenarios (see attached: redwood_commitment_scenarios_v2.xlsx) plus a working MAP (mutual-action-plan-apexbio.docx). High-level summary below; workbook has the math and estimated monthly spend.

Quick summary of our proposed staging plan:

1) Starter (Q1 ramp) — conservative commit for baseline shop: 4 x H100 80GB-equivalent slots (reserved), supports ~250 concurrent gen requests at small batch sizes with P95 token latency target ~140ms under steady-state. Good for proof-of-concept and initial traffic.

2) Production (Q2–Q4) — 12 x A100 80GB-equivalent + 6 x L4 for embedding offload (reserved), with 25% burst pool on H100s for peak periods. This configuration targets your 2.5M tokens/day plus 3x short bursts and keeps end-to-end P95 within 300–350ms for typical prompt lengths.

3) Scale (12–24 months) — mix increases to 20 x A100-equivalent + flexible H100 pool for low-latency tiers + additional L4s for embeddings, plus autoscaling to private-burst capacity during scheduled batch windows.

Key assumptions we used (called out in the workbook):
- Average token compute cost mapped from model family (chat model dense 33B approximated to ~0.28 TFLOP per token on A100 perf profile).
- Batch sizes: steady-state 1–4 tokens, batch-optimized workers for embedding throughput.
- KV cache hit rate assumptions: 15% prefix reuse on conversational flows.

Questions for you before we finalize:
- Do you have an SLO boundary that requires end-to-end latency rather than token latency? We modeled both, but the choice changes the mix.
- Any constraints on acceptable quantization or perf degradation (you mentioned some internal QA for hallucination sensitivity)?

Next steps: Connor will coordinate a 60-minute workshop to align workload traces and pin the final commit tiers. We can include a short performance run using a sampled trace.

Available times: tomorrow 10:00–12:00 PST or Thursday 14:00–16:00 PST.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFP: Commitment scenarios for dedicated inference (ApexBio) — GPU mix recommendation

Lauren / Maya —

Adding a technical recommendation to the staging plan Lauren shared. I focused on throughput per-GPU, latency expectations, and fallback routing rules. Attached: gpu-mix-suggestion.csv (simple throughput matrix).

Short recommendations:
- Latency-critical gen (single-turn, low tolerance for staleness): map to H100-class reserved slices where possible. H100 gives ~20–35% lower p99 token latency vs A100 on attention-heavy sequences. Reserve ~30% of production tier on H100s.
- Bulk gen and cost-optimized tiers: A100 80GB-equivalent gives better token cost for sustained throughput. Use A100 for the core reserved capacity.
- Embedding and high-batch offline jobs: L4 or comparable Ampere T4-class instances; these are cheaper and can be scaled independently.

Throughput & reservation mapping (rough figures; full math in CSV):
- 1 H100 slot (optimized) -> ~1.6M tokens/day mixed workload equivalent (low-latency profile).
- 1 A100 80GB-equiv -> ~900k tokens/day mixed workload.
- 1 L4 -> 1.2M embedding vectors/hour (batch).

Burst policy and graceful degradation:
- Primary routing: reserved pool by model tag (chat-v33b, embed-v-small).
- If reserved capacity exhausted: route non-latency-sensitive requests to A100 burst pool (pre-warmed), and if still saturated, route to hosted fallback model (lighter quantized variant) with explicit header informing application and incremented quota burn.
- SLO protection: for requests flagged latency-critical, automatic failover to a dedicated low-latency lane (H100) that is sized with a 15% buffer to reduce cross-tenant variance.

Operational notes:
- Provisioning lead time: H100 pools typically need 7–10 business days for reserved capacity; A100 can be provisioned in 2–3 days depending on region.
- Quantization constraints: we recommend FP16 or Q4_K for chat models; if your QA requires FP32-like fidelity we need to revisit commit sizes.

Happy to walk through the CSV in the workshop.

—Karthik
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
